case_source: (From the judgment and order dated 26.02.2007 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No.557 of 1997)
full_judgment:
Syed Mahmud Hossain J. This appeal by leave is directed against the judgment and order dated 26.02.2007 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 557 of 1997 making the Rule absolute.

2. The facts, leading to the filing of this appeal, in a nutshell, are:

<u>3. The predecessors of appellant No.1 herein as the plaintiff instituted Other Suit No. 30 of 1991 in the Fifth Court of Assistant Judge, Sadar, Chittagong for a decree of declaration of the plaintiffs title over the suit schedule-1 land measuring .38 acre and also for declaration that the plaintiffs were entitled to receive the compensation money for the requisition of schedule-1(Ka) land under schedule-1, measuring .26 acre and the principal-defendants have no right in that.</u>

4. The plaintiffs' case, in short, is that the suit land belonged to one Gani Mia, who sold the same land by a registered deed of sale dated 05.05.1925 to Lal Mia. After that, Lal Mia sold the same by a registered deed of sale dated 16.06.1925 to Najir Ahmed, the father of the plaintiffs. Subsequently, Najir Ahmed settled the said land with Abdur Rahman by a registered patta. Abdur Rahman used to stay in Burma. During the R.S operation, the R.S. Khatian for the suit land was recorded in the names of the plaintiffs father, Najir Ahmed and his four brothers, though they had no title to the suit land and they also did not possess the land on the basis of the wrong recording. Abdur Rahman sold the suit land to the plaintiff by a registered deed of sale dated 15.02.1975 and the plaintiffs are in possession of the suit land. The recent B.S. Khatian was recorded in their names. Proforma defendant Nos.11 and 12 acquired 0.26 acre of land described in schedule 1(Ka) in L.A. Case No.13 of 1986-87. A Compensation Assessment Roll was duly prepared in the names of the plaintiffs. The principal defendants taking the advantage of the wrong recording of the land in R.S. and P.S. Khatians raised objection against the plaintiffs' right to get compensation for the acquired land and as such, the suit was filed to remove the cloud in the suit land.

5. Defendant Nos.2-8 contested the suit by filing written statement denying all the material statements made in the plaint of the suit. Their case, in short, is that the suit land belonged to C.S. recorded tenant Oli Mia, who by an amicable partition with Gani Mia was in possession of the suit land and subsequently, Oli Mia died leaving behind 5 sons namely, Najir Ahmed and his four brothers and the R.S. record was rightly made in their names. Abdur Rahman, son of Oli Mia, sold 0.08 acre of suit land to this defendant by a registered deed of sale dated 28.05.1986 and out of said land 0.05 acre was acquired by the Government and that mutation khatian in respect of 0.08 acre of suit land was prepared in the name of the defendant. The plaintiffs father, Najir Ahmed was entitled to get share in the suit land and that the alleged deeds of transfer and the deed of settlement are forged and ineffective and Najir Ahmed had never possessed the suit land.

6. The trial Court, upon hearing the par-ties, by the judgment and decree dated 11.11.1991 dismissed the suit.

7. Against the judgment and decree passed by the trial court, the plaintiffs preferred Other Appeal No.706 of 1991 before the learned District Judge, Chittagong. On transfer, the appeal was heard and disposed of by the then learned Subordinate Judge, Second Court and Artha Rin Adalat, Chittagong, who upon hearing the appeal, by the judgment and decree dated 05.08.1996 allowed the appeal setting aside the judgment and decree passed by the trial Court.

8. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with judgment and decree passed by the appellate Court, the defendants moved the High Court Division by filing a revisional application and obtained Rule in Civil Revision No.557 of 1997. The learned Single Judge of the High Court Division upon hearing both the sides by the judgment and order dated 26.02.2007 made the Rule absolute.

9. Feeling aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the judgment and order passed by the High Court Division, the plaintiffs as the leave-petitioners have filed Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No.1864 of 2007 before this Division and obtained leave on 24.07.2008 resulting in Civil Appeal No. 67 of 2009.

10. Mr. Mahbubey Alam, learned Senior Advocate, appearing on behalf of the appellants, submits that the High Court Division committed error in dismissing the suit without adverting to the findings arrived at by the Court of appeal which decreed the suit on consideration of possession of the predecessor-in-interest of the plaintiffs and as such, the impugned judgment should be set aside. He further submits that the High Court Division erred in law in applying the amended provision of section 107 of the Transfer of Property Act and in the instant case lease had been granted by the landlord by executing and registering a patta in the year 1925 and that execution of a lease deed, by the lessor as well as by the lessee was not mandatory before 1929. He then submits that the Court of appeal below decreed the suit by taking into consideration that Abdur Rahman was in possession of the suit land on the strength of the patta executed by the Nazir Ahmed and that as soon as the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act came into force, he became a rayiat under the Government and thus while making the Rule absolute, the High Court Division failed to consider the aforesaid finding of the appellate Court. He lastly submits that the High Court Division committed error in rejecting exhibit-3, the registered patta dated 18.07.1925 by the landlord treating the same as a lease deed under section 107 of the Transfer of Property Act and committed error in not considering that when the Bengal Tenancy Act was in operation, the landlord had authority to grant patta in respect of the suit land and a patta is always a document executed only by the landlord under the then circumstances.

11. Mr. Kamal-ul-Alam, learned Senior Advocate, appearing on behalf of the respondents, on the other hand, submits that the trial Court as well as the High Court Division on meticulous consideration of the materials on record, came to the finding that the plaintiffs could not prove their title to and possession in the suit land and as such, no interference is called for.

12. We have considered the submissions of the learned Senior Advocates of both the sides, perused the impugned judgment and the materials on record.

<u>13. The trial Court came to the finding that on consideration of evidence on record, it appeared that the plaintiff could not prove that at the time of R.S. operation, Abdur Rahman was in Burma (now Myanmar). The trial Court also came to the finding that the plaintiff could not prove that Abdur Rahman possessed the suit land himself or through 'bargader' and as such, the contention of the plaintiff-appellants that taking advantage of Abdur Rahman's staying in Burma, the R.S. khatian was wrongly prepared in the names of Nazir Ahmed and his four brothers. The trial court also found that exhibits-2, 2ka and 3 were never acted upon. The trial Court, therefore, concluded that the plaintiffs had failed to prove their title to and possession in the suit land.</u>

14. The appellate Court, on the other hand, came to the finding that as per C.S. khatian Gani Mia (Guno Mia) was in exclusive possession of plot No.3182. The Appellate Court also found that in the C.S. khatian the four boundaries of the plot were clearly given which exclusively proved that Gani Mia, the C.S. recorded tenant was in exclusive possession of the suit plot No.3182. The appellate Court held that the suit land did not belong to Oli Mia but that it actually belonged to Gani Mia, who sold it to Lal Mia, who again sold it to Najir Ahmed. The Appellate Court also held that as Najir Ahmed had succeeded in proving his title by way of purchase on the basis of registered deed (exhibit-2ka) the initial presumption attached to R.S. khatian, exhibit-1(ka) was rebutted. The appellate Court also held that Najir Ahmed as tenure-holder in R.S. plot No.4429 (suit plot) was entitled to transfer the same by way of settlement which he did accordingly by executing patta exhibit-3 dated 18.07.1925, by which 18 gondas of land were transferred to Abdur Rahman. The appellate Court also held that the allegations of fraud by Najir Ahmed was not proved by cogent evidence and that the appellate Court also held that one who alleged fraud must bear the burden of proving it and the burden is comparatively heavier when it is against old registered documents. The appellate Court also held that by three documents (exhibits-2, 2ka and 3) no land of Oli Mia was attracted and that the chance of fraud in view of the given circumstances seemed to be too remote. Therefore, the appellate Court concluded that the plaintiffs had been able to prove their title to and possession in the suit land and accordingly, the appellate Court decreed the suit.

15. The High Court Division concurred with the findings arrived at by the trial Court and held that the appellate Court was not justified in reversing the findings of the fact arrived at by the trial Court. The High Court Division held that as the suit land was settled permanently, it was required to be registered under section 107 of the Transfer of the Property Act and that the patta was not executed by the ten-ant Abdur Rahman and as such, it was not valid in the eye of law.

16. The High Court Division also found that the plaintiffs could not prove their title on the basis of exhibits-2, 2ka and 3 and also possession in the suit land. Therefore, the High Court Division made the Rule absolute setting aside the judgment and decree delivered by the appellate Court concurring with the judgment and decree passed by the trial Court.

17. The plaintiffs claimed that land of C.S. khatian No.3182 belonged to Gani Mia who sold it to Lal Mia by a registered deed of sale dated 05.05.1925. Lal Mia also sold the land of the said plot to Najir Ahmed by a registered deed of sale dated 16.06.1925. Najir Ahmed settled the suit land to Abdur Rahman by a registered patta dated 18.07.1925. Abdur Rahman owned and possessed the suit land by paying rent to Najir Ahmed, the predecessor of the plaintiffs. But during S.A. operation, the land of said patta was wrongly recorded in the names of Najir Ahmed and his four brothers as Abdur Rahman at the relevant time was in Burma. Subsequently, Abdur Rahman sold the suit land as shown in schedule-Ka to the plaint to the plaintiffs by a registered deed of sale dated 15.02.1975.

18. On the other hand, the defendants claimed that their predecessor Oli Mia was the recorded tenant of C. S. khatian and that Oli Mia by amicable settlement with Gani Mia got the suit land as shown in the 1st schedule to the plaint and that he died leaving behind Najir Ahmed, Sadik Ahmed, Abdur Rahman, Abdul Khaleque and Md. Nasir. Subsequently, the suit land was correctly recorded in the names of Najir Ahmed and his four brothers. Najir Ahmed was the owner of 1/5th share of the suit land. In order to deprive his brothers, Najir Ahmed collusively created the deeds dated 05.05.1925 and 16.06.1925 and that those documents were not acted upon. The registered patta dated 18.07.1925 standing in the name of Abdur Rahman is also collusive. Therefore, the claim of the plaintiffs on the basis of registered deed of sale dated 15.02.1975 is void, collusive, inoperative and without any consideration.

19. Abdur Rahman, son of Oli Mia, sold .08 acre of land to the defendants by a registered deed of sale dated 28.05.1986. The 1st schedule land to the plaint has been recorded in C.S. plot No.3182 corresponding to R.S. plot No.4429. The C.S. record, exhibit-1 shows that the recorded tenants were Gani Mia, Oli Mia and Karimjan. The C. S. record (exhibit-1) reveals that the recorded tenants were in specific possession of the different plots of the khatian. Oli Mia was in possession of C.S. Plot Nos.3114 and 3380. Gani Mia was in specific in C.S. plot Nos.3182 and 3184 and the remaining plots were possessed by Karimjan. In the C.S. Khatian four boundaries of plots were clearly given so as to denote actual possession of each of the tenants. C.S. plot No.3182 exclusively stands in the names of the Gani Mia which is bounded on north by a road and on the south and east by Oli Miah and on the western side by Abul Hossain. Therefore, the aforesaid entry in C.S. khatian proved possession of Gani Mia, the C. S. recorded tenant exclusively in C. S. plot No.3182 and his title to the said plot would follow from the established possession. Gani Mia as an exclusive owner sold 18 gondas of land of C.S. plot No.3182 to Lal Mia by giving a defined boundary on 05.05.1925. Out of 96 decimals of the C.S. plot, 36 decimals of land were transferred which is proved by exhibit-2. While in possession of the said land, Lal Mia sold it to Najir Ahmed by a registered deed of sale dated 16.06.1925 (exhibit-2ka) and handed over possession thereof.

<u>20. The aforesaid findings proved that the suit land did not belong to Oli Mia but it actually belonged to Gani Mia, who sold it to Lal Mia, who again sold it to Najir Ahmed. As Najir Ahmed has succeeded in proving his title by way of purchase on the basis of registered deed (exhibit-2ka) the initial presumption attached to the R.S. khatian exhibit-1(ka) was rebutted. Therefore, Najir Ahmed was legally entitle to settled the suit land to Abdur Rahman by exhibit-3, the registered patta dated 18.07.1925. The appellate Court on consideration of evidence on record found that the allegation of fraud was not proved in obtaining the suit land by the plaintiffs. The appellate Court also discussed the evidence adduced by P.Ws.1, 2 and 3 and found that they could prove that the Abdur Rahman was in actual possession of the suit land. The appellate Court also noted that P.Ws.2 and 3 were not cross-examined by the defendants in respect of their evidence as regards possession of the plaintiffs in the suit land. The appellate Court also noted that the defendants did not adduce any oral or documentary evidence during the trial. The appellate Court also considered exhibits-4 and 4ka, the rent receipts in respect of the suit land and found that the plaintiffs paid rent before filing of the suit and that rent receipt not only proved possession of the plaintiffs but also proved as collateral evidence of title to the suit land. The appellate Court noted that respondent No.3 filed three rent receipts relating to P.S. plot No.3080 for an area of .08, .22, .10 and .05 acre of land and that from those rent receipts, the plaintiffs' claim of possession was not affected so far as regards the quantum of land in P.S. khatian No.3082. The appellate Court also held that the defendants had not come out with positive proof regarding exclusive possession of P.S. plot No.4429 and as such, their onus was not discharged.</u>

<u>21. The High Court Division came to the finding that the patta dated 18.07.1925 should have been a bilateral document and that it should have been executed by both the landlord Najir Ahmed and tenant Abdur Rahman and as such, it was not valid according to section 107 of the Transfer of Property Act. This finding of the High Court Division is erroneous as the patta, exhibit-3 dated 18.07.1925 was executed and registered before 1929. A lease deed is required to be executed and registered by both the tenant and landlord under section 107 of the Transfer of Property Act on and from 1929.</u>

22. In the light of the findings made before, we find substance in this appeal. Accordingly, the appeal is allowed and the judgment delivered by the High Court Division is set aside and the judgment and decree passed by the appellate Court is restored.

23. There is not order as to costs.

End.
